questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The intense purple color of aqueous potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$) arises from
optionsEn: a ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) transition from filled $\text{O}(2p)$ orbitals to empty $\text{Mn}(3d)$ orbitals
a metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) transition from $\text{Mn}(3d)$ to $\text{O}(\pi^*)$
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{MnO}_4^-$, manganese is in the $+7$ oxidation state ($3d^0$), so no $d\text{--}d$ or MLCT transitions are possible. The intense purple color ($\varepsilon \approx 2400\text{ L mol}^{-1}\text{ cm}^{-1}$) is due to a fully allowed (spin- and Laporte-allowed) $\text{O}(2p) \to \text{Mn}(3d)$ LMCT transition.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Among the following octahedral aqua complexes, the one that exhibits the strongest static Jahn–Teller distortion is
questions.explanationEn: Strong static Jahn–Teller distortion occurs when the antibonding $e_g$ orbitals are unequally occupied. In $[\text{Cu(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$ ($d^9$, $t_{2g}^6 e_g^3$), the $e_g$ set is unsymmetrically filled ($^2E_g$ ground state), causing pronounced tetragonal elongation. By contrast, $d^8$ ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^2$), $d^3$ ($t_{2g}^3$), and high-spin $d^5$ ($t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$) are orbitally non-degenerate.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: When a radioactive nuclide emits one $\alpha$-particle followed by two $\beta^-$-particles in succession, the resulting daughter nuclide is an **isotope** of the parent nuclide because
optionsEn: its mass number $A$ decreases by $4$ while its atomic number $Z$ returns to the original value
both its mass number $A$ and atomic number $Z$ remain unchanged
its mass number $A$ increases by $4$ while its atomic number $Z$ decreases by $2$
its neutron number $N$ remains unchanged while $Z$ increases by $2$
questions.explanationEn: One $\alpha$ emission changes $(A, Z) \to (A-4, Z-2)$. Two subsequent $\beta^-$ emissions change $(A-4, Z-2) \to (A-4, Z)$. Since the daughter has the same $Z$ as the parent but a different $A$, they are isotopes.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Chlorophyll-$a$ contains a central metal ion coordinated to four nitrogens of a reduced porphyrin (chlorin) ring. The metal ion is
questions.explanationEn: Chlorophylls contain a $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ion at the center of a chlorin macrocycle (a porphyrin ring in which one pyrrole double bond is reduced).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: According to the spectrochemical series, the correct increasing order of ligand field strength ($\Delta_o$) is
questions.explanationEn: In the spectrochemical series, $\pi$-donor halides are weak-field ligands, $\sigma$-donors like $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{NH}_3$ are intermediate, and $\pi$-acceptor ligands like $\text{CN}^-$ and $\text{CO}$ are strong-field ligands: $\text{I}^- < \text{Cl}^- < \text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{NH}_3 < \text{CN}^-$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The octahedral complex $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_3(\text{NO}_2)_3]$ exists as two geometrical isomers, *fac* and *mer*. Their respective point-group symmetries are
questions.explanationEn: In the *fac* (facial) isomer of $\text{MA}_3\text{B}_3$, the three $\text{A}$ ligands occupy one triangular face of the octahedron and the three $\text{B}$ ligands occupy the opposite face, giving $C_{3v}$ symmetry. In the *mer* (meridional) isomer, the three $\text{A}$ ligands lie in a meridian plane passing through the metal, giving $C_{2v}$ symmetry.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Vanadium hexacarbonyl, $\text{V(CO)}_6$, is a blue-black crystalline solid that is an exception to the $18$-electron rule. Which one of the following statements about $\text{V(CO)}_6$ is **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: It is a $17$-electron paramagnetic monomer that readily accepts one electron to form the stable $18$-electron anion $[\text{V(CO)}_6]^-$.
It dimerizes spontaneously at room temperature to form diamagnetic $\text{V}_2(\text{CO})_{12}$.
It is a $19$-electron radical that readily loses one electron to form $[\text{V(CO)}_6]^+$.
It has a trigonal prismatic geometry with $3$ unpaired electrons.
questions.explanationEn: Neutral $\text{V}$ ($5\text{ e}^-$) $+ 6\,\text{CO}$ ($12\text{ e}^-$) $= 17\text{ e}^-$ ($1$ unpaired electron, paramagnetic). Dimerization to $\text{V}_2(\text{CO})_{12}$ would require sterically unfavorable $7$-coordination around $\text{V}$, so $\text{V(CO)}_6$ remains monomeric and acts as a strong one-electron oxidant to form the $18$-electron anion $[\text{V(CO)}_6]^-$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: When an octahedral $d^9$ complex $[\text{Cu(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$ undergoes tetragonal elongation along the $z$-axis ($z$-out Jahn–Teller distortion), the resulting energy ordering of the $3d$ orbitals from lowest to highest is
questions.explanationEn: Moving the two axial ligands outward along $\pm z$ decreases electrostatic repulsion for all orbitals with a $z$-component ($d_{z^2}, d_{xz}, d_{yz}$) and increases it for in-plane orbitals ($d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{xy}$). In moderate tetragonal elongation (unlike extreme square planar), $d_{z^2}$ remains above $d_{xy}$: $d_{xz} = d_{yz} < d_{xy} < d_{z^2} < d_{x^2-y^2}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Among the $3d$ metallocenes ferrocene ($\text{FeCp}_2$), cobaltocene ($\text{CoCp}_2$), and nickelocene ($\text{NiCp}_2$), the metal–ring carbon ($\text{M}-\text{C}$) bond length increases in the order
questions.explanationEn: $\text{FeCp}_2$ ($18\text{ e}^-$) fills all bonding and non-bonding MOs up to $a_{1g}'$ and $e_{2g}$. In $\text{CoCp}_2$ ($19\text{ e}^-$) and $\text{NiCp}_2$ ($20\text{ e}^-$), the extra $1$ and $2$ electrons occupy the metal–ligand antibonding $e_{1g}^*$ orbitals, progressively weakening and lengthening the $\text{M}-\text{C}$ bond: $\text{FeCp}_2$ ($206\text{ pm}$) $< \text{CoCp}_2$ ($212\text{ pm}$) $< \text{NiCp}_2$ ($220\text{ pm}$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the Orgel diagram for complexes having $F$ ground free-ion terms ($^3F$ or $^4F$), which of the following pairs of metal-ion configurations have the **same** splitting pattern with an $A_2$ (or $A_{2g}$) ground state?
questions.explanationEn: In the $F$-term Orgel diagram, the $A_2$/$A_{2g}$ ground state occurs on the side corresponding to $d^3$ (oct), $d^8$ (oct), $d^2$ (tet), and $d^7$ (tet). By contrast, $d^2$ (oct), $d^7$ (oct), $d^3$ (tet), and $d^8$ (tet) have a $T_1$/$T_{1g}$ ground state.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding oxidative addition and reductive elimination is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: Oxidative addition is favored by electron-rich, coordinatively unsaturated low-valent metal centers (such as $16\text{ e}^-$ $d^8$ $\text{Rh(I)}$ or $\text{Ir(I)}$).
Oxidative addition of $\text{H}_2$ to a square-planar $d^8$ complex proceeds via a concerted three-center transition state yielding a *cis*-dihydride product.
Reductive elimination is accelerated by bulky ancillary ligands (large cone angle) and electron-poor metal centers.
Oxidative addition decreases the coordination number of the metal by $2$.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A), (B), (C) are all true.
- (D) False: Oxidative addition *increases* both the coordination number and formal oxidation state of the metal by $2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about transition metal nitrosyl complexes is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: A linear $\text{M}-\text{N}-\text{O}$ linkage generally exhibits a higher $\nu_{\text{NO}}$ stretching wavenumber ($\sim 1650\text{--}1950\text{ cm}^{-1}$) than a bent $\text{M}-\text{N}-\text{O}$ linkage ($\sim 1525\text{--}1720\text{ cm}^{-1}$).
$[\text{Co(CO)}_3(\text{NO})]$ is an $18$-electron tetrahedral complex containing a linear nitrosyl ligand.
$[\text{Fe(CO)}_2(\text{NO})_2]$ is isoelectronic with $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$ and obeys the $18$-electron rule with two linear nitrosyl ligands.
A bent $\text{M}-\text{N}-\text{O}$ ligand donates more electrons than a linear $\text{M}-\text{N}-\text{O}$ ligand.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: Linear $\text{NO}^+$ has a higher $\text{N}-\text{O}$ bond order than bent $\text{NO}^-$.
- (B) True: $\text{Co}(9) + 3\,\text{CO}(6) + \text{NO}_{\text{linear}}(3) = 18\text{ e}^-$.
- (C) True: $\text{Fe}(8) + 2\,\text{CO}(4) + 2\,\text{NO}_{\text{linear}}(6) = 18\text{ e}^-$, isoelectronic with $\text{Ni(CO)}_4$.
- (D) False: Linear $\text{NO}$ donates $3\text{ e}^-$ (neutral method), whereas bent $\text{NO}$ donates only $1\text{ e}^-$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about EDTA complexometric titrations is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: The fully deprotonated ligand $\text{EDTA}^{4-}$ is hexadentate, coordinating via two tertiary amine nitrogens and four carboxylate oxygens.
The conditional formation constant $K_f' = \alpha_{\text{Y}^{4-}} K_f$ increases with increasing $\text{pH}$ because a larger fraction of EDTA exists as $\text{Y}^{4-}$.

Cyanide ion ($\text{CN}^-$) can be used as a masking agent to prevent interference from $\text{Ni}^{2+}$, $\text{Cu}^{2+}$, and $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ when titrating $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ or $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ with EDTA.
EDTA forms $1:2$ (metal : EDTA) complexes with trivalent ions like $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ and $\text{Al}^{3+}$.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A), (B), (C) are all true.
- (D) False: Regardless of metal charge ($+2, +3,$ or $+4$), EDTA invariably forms $1:1$ complexes ($[\text{M(EDTA)}]^{n-4}$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about the zinc metalloenzymes carbonic anhydrase and carboxypeptidase A is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: In both enzymes, the catalytic $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ion is coordinated in a distorted tetrahedral geometry in the resting state.
In carbonic anhydrase, $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ is bound to three histidine residues and one water/hydroxide ligand.
In carboxypeptidase A, $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ is bound to two histidine residues, one glutamate carboxylate, and one water molecule.
Replacing $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ with $\text{Co}^{2+}$ completely destroys catalytic activity in both enzymes.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A), (B), (C) are all true.
- (D) False: $\text{Co}^{2+}$-substituted carbonic anhydrase and carboxypeptidase A retain substantial catalytic activity and are widely used as spectroscopic ($d\text{--}d$ and EPR) probes of the active site.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The spin-only magnetic moment of high-spin $[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$ is _______ $\mu_B$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn:
$\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ($3d^4$) with weak-field $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is high-spin ($t_{2g}^3 e_g^1$) with $n = 4$ unpaired electrons.
$\mu_s = \sqrt{4(4+2)}\,\mu_B = \sqrt{24}\,\mu_B \approx 4.90\,\mu_B$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The spin multiplicity ($2S + 1$) of the ground-state Russell–Saunders term for a free $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ($3d^3$) ion is _______.
questions.explanationEn: In $3d^3$, all $3$ electrons have parallel spins ($S = 3 \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{2}$), so $2S + 1 = 2(\frac{3}{2}) + 1 = 4$ (quartet, $^4F$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: According to the $18$-electron rule, the total number of $\text{Fe}-\text{Fe}$ single bonds in the triangular cluster $\text{Fe}_3(\text{CO})_{12}$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Total valence electrons (TVE) $= 3(8) + 12(2) = 48\text{ e}^-$. Number of $\text{Fe}-\text{Fe}$ bonds $= \frac{18(3) - 48}{2} = \frac{54 - 48}{2} = 3$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of stereoisomers (including optical isomers) possible for the octahedral complex ion $[\text{Co(en)}_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn: $[\text{Co(en)}_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ has $1$ achiral *trans* isomer and $1$ *cis* isomer that exists as a pair of enantiomers ($\Delta$ and $\Lambda$), giving $1 + 2 = 3$ stereoisomers in total.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of unpaired electrons on the iron center in deoxy-myoglobin (high-spin $\text{Fe}^{2+}$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Deoxy-myoglobin contains $5$-coordinate high-spin $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ($3d^6$, $S = 2$), which has $4$ unpaired electrons.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry II: Coordination, Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The neutral dinuclear iron carbonyl $[\text{Fe}_2(\text{CO})_x]$ contains one $\text{Fe}-\text{Fe}$ single bond and obeys the $18$-electron rule at each iron atom. The integer value of $x$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn:
For two $\text{Fe}$ atoms ($2 \times 8 = 16\text{ e}^-$), one $\text{Fe}-\text{Fe}$ bond ($2\text{ e}^-$ shared), and $x$ $\text{CO}$ ligands ($2x\text{ e}^-$) to reach $2 \times 18 = 36\text{ e}^-$:
$16 + 2x + 2 = 36 \implies 2x = 18 \implies x = 9$ (i.e., $\text{Fe}_2(\text{CO})_9$).
